instruction: Search earlier evidence by exact reference first, then verify pinned official source scope and task mode. Preserve holds and do not accept mappings from shared wording.

originalTask.draftLearningTask: Trace a specimen from clinical question through diagnosis and explain how pathology informs management.
Define common pathology terms and identify milestones in the discipline's development.
Map cell-cycle checkpoints and explain how stem cells support repair and regenerative medicine.
Classify major insults and link mechanisms of injury to cellular and clinical consequences.
Compare mechanisms and morphological changes that distinguish reversible injury from irreversible injury.
Distinguish lipid, protein, carbohydrate and pigment accumulation on representative images.
Compare mechanisms and morphology of necrosis, apoptosis and autolysis.
Compare dystrophic and metastatic calcification and distinguish representative patterns of gangrene.
Compare atrophy, hypertrophy, hyperplasia and metaplasia, then distinguish dysplasia from carcinoma in situ.
Explain how cumulative damage, senescence and apoptotic pathways affect cellular ageing.
Identify patterns of injury on gross and microscopic specimens and explain their likely consequences.
Compare triggers, vascular changes and cellular responses across acute and chronic inflammation.
Group major mediators by source and relate them to vascular and cellular effects.
Compare causes and features of nonspecific and granulomatous inflammation and give representative examples.
Identify acute and chronic inflammation in gross and microscopic examples and justify each classification.
Compare regeneration and scarring and sequence healing by primary and secondary intention.
Classify oedema by mechanism and relate hydrostatic, oncotic, permeability and lymphatic changes to representative presentations.
Distinguish active hyperaemia from passive congestion and classify representative haemorrhage patterns.
Compare major causes of circulatory failure and explain the progression from compensation to irreversible injury.
Trace normal haemostasis and use Virchow's triad to explain thrombus formation and outcomes.
Distinguish the three processes and relate causes and embolus type to distribution, morphology and clinical effects.
Identify gross and microscopic features of representative infarcts and explain how tissue and timing affect appearance.
Classify neoplasms by lineage and compare benign and malignant tumours by gross and microscopic features, behaviour and routes of spread.
Use breast and colorectal examples to explain how driver mutations, tumour suppressor loss and epigenetic changes contribute to progression.
Classify chemical, physical and biological carcinogens and compare mechanisms by which they initiate or promote cancer.
Distinguish local and metastatic effects from systemic effects and explain representative paraneoplastic syndromes.
Compare tissue diagnosis, molecular profiling and tumour markers by purpose and limitations, and discuss an emerging diagnostic approach.
Explain immune recognition and escape and relate these mechanisms to the rationale for representative immunotherapies.
Identify gross and microscopic features in representative benign and malignant specimens and justify each classification.
Compare sample collection, preparation and staining methods and explain when cytology can inform care or requires tissue confirmation.
Compare innate and adaptive responses and trace antigen recognition, activation and effector mechanisms.
Classify reactions by mechanism and link each major type to representative tissue injury.
Explain HLA matching and compare the immune mechanisms of hyperacute, acute and chronic rejection.
Explain loss of self-tolerance and compare mechanisms in representative organ-specific and systemic autoimmune diseases.
Trace loss of tolerance, autoantibody formation and immune-complex injury and relate them to representative organ lesions.
Trace target-cell infection and immune depletion and relate them to characteristic tissue changes and complications.
Explain fibril formation and compare the causes, distribution and consequences of major forms of amyloid deposition.
Identify representative gross and microscopic deposits, interpret Congo red findings and connect the affected organs to clinical consequences.
Relate erythrocyte infection, haemolysis and sequestration to representative organ pathology.
Trace tissue larval deposition and explain how cyst location and degeneration influence inflammation and injury.
Compare tissue and nerve changes across the leprosy spectrum and relate them to host immunity and organism burden.
Compare representative bacterial, viral, protozoal and helminthic diseases by route of injury, host response and tissue morphology.
Relate viral and host responses to representative pulmonary and systemic lesions and interpret characteristic laboratory findings in context.
Compare representative chromosomal abnormalities and pathogenic variants by mechanism and phenotype and select suitable diagnostic modalities.
Compare representative childhood tumours and tumour-like lesions by developmental origin, typical age, site and morphology.
Link representative enzyme defects to accumulated substrates and explain their organ-specific consequences.
Relate air pollution, tobacco, alcohol and noise exposure to distinct mechanisms of tissue injury and representative disorders.
Compare tissue and metabolic responses to protein–calorie malnutrition, vitamin deficiencies and starvation.
Explain how adipose dysfunction and insulin resistance contribute to metabolic syndrome and downstream organ injury.
Compare marrow and extramedullary blood formation and explain anticoagulant choice in haematology.
Classify anaemia by indices and mechanism and construct an initial investigation sequence.
Demonstrate collection workflow and identify appropriate tubes, additives and instruments.
Measure haemoglobin and red and white cell counts and perform a differential using approved samples.
Trace iron metabolism and distinguish common microcytic causes using indices and iron studies.
Identify microcytosis and hypochromia on a smear and describe accompanying findings.
Explain B12 handling and deficiency and select tests for macrocytic anaemia.
Distinguish megaloblastic from other macrocytic patterns using causes and laboratory features.
Identify macrocytic patterns and report macro-ovalocytes or hypersegmented neutrophils when present.
Classify haemolysis and explain how its site and mechanism affect findings and indices.
Compare pathogenesis, indices, smear findings and distinguishing clinical features.
